modules.description: Arithmetic operation signatures and their fixities, including NonZero divisors and InRange refinements.
Bit operations, shifts, and the corresponding operator/fixity vocabulary.
Group-style inverse/subtraction vocabulary over admitted carrier instances.
Identity plus combination vocabulary, default folding, and unit laws with explicit checking status.
Associative combination vocabulary and its law. Reported finite checks are distinct from universal proofs.
Zero/one and additive/multiplicative structure, with its law vocabulary.
Empty and choice operations for admitted higher-kinded containers.
Container application and value lifting for independent structure-preserving composition.
Generic folds, conversion to lists, size/emptiness, and related operations over container instances.
Higher-kinded mapping vocabulary, distinct from the lexical do-sequencing provider mechanism.
Container-dependent composition through the admitted higher-kinded class vocabulary.
Generic effect/container-aware traversal and sequencing while retaining the input shape.
AES-128/192/256 with AES-NI or ARMv8 instructions after detection and a constant-time, table-free SIMD fallback.
ChaCha20 and XChaCha20 streams, Poly1305 and the ChaCha20-Poly1305 and XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs with vector row kernels.
CTR, OFB, CFB, CBC and GCM over any 128-bit block cipher, with constant-time or carry-less-instruction GHASH and constant-time tag checks.
Branch-free scalar comparison and selection, full-input byte equality, conditional copying and in-place XOR with public bounds and atomic length errors.
DES and Triple DES block ciphers with ECB, CBC and CTR for legacy interoperation, from a generated straight-line round kernel.
Deterministic (RFC 6979) and hedged P-256 ECDSA signatures in raw and DER form with strict verification.
Deterministic Ed25519 signatures with constant-time signing and strict verification.
Constant-time arithmetic modulo 2^255 - 19 with 128-bit column products, shared by X25519 and Ed25519.
Prepared HMAC-SHA-256/SHA-512 keys, persistent messages and full-tag verification.
Hybrid public key encryption (RFC 9180) over DHKEM X25519 and P-256, HKDF and AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305, in all four modes.
HKDF and PBKDF2 key derivation with checked lengths, binary inputs and HMAC-SHA-256.
FIPS 204 ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87 post-quantum digital signatures: deterministic and hedged signing, verification, and key/signature codecs.
ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024 key encapsulation (FIPS 203) with branch-free SIMD lane kernels.
Constant-time NIST P-256 keys, SEC 1 point encodings, ECDH and scalar/point arithmetic over generated Montgomery kernels.
PKIX distinguished names, OIDs, RFC 4514 formatting, algorithm identifiers, X.509 extensions, times and certificate revocation lists (CRLs).
The RC4 stream cipher as a persistent keystream state, for legacy data only.
RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS signing/verification, OAEP and PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption/decryption, PKCS#1 DER key codecs and seeded key generation.
Pure sans-I/O RFC 8446 TLS 1.3 client and server handshake state machine, key schedule, record AEAD framing, ALPN/SNI and X.509 verification.
Constant-time X25519 Diffie-Hellman key agreement with low-order peer rejection.
X.509 v3 certificate parsing, creation and chain verification, RFC 6125 hostname and IP SAN checks, CSRs, and PKIX/PKCS#8/SEC1/PKCS#1 key codecs.
Checked immutable array range edits, predicate deletion, adjacent compaction, reversal and concatenation.
Packed scalar constructors for Array. The element format travels with the buffer, so generic reads and updates keep it.
Immutable array comparison, indexed lookups, binary search and sortedness with explicit callback policies.
Immutable contiguous arrays with optional failed reads, updates, slices, and ranges, plus list conversions.
ASCII-refined values and checked construction at text boundaries.
Decimal arithmetic with explicit precision/scale and rounding/error behaviour in the exported API.
Boolean operations and their comparison instances.
Fresh byte cloning, doubling repetition, concatenation and separator-aware joining.
Nonempty raw-byte field views with Unicode whitespace, ordered scalar predicates, persistent producers and replayable effect-preserving iteration.
Exact first, last, containment and count queries over raw bytes with bounded SWAR traversals.
Retained byte splitting, persistent producer traversals, shared pull cursors and line iteration.
Raw UTF-8 validation, forward and reverse decoding, scalar counting, fresh repair and atomic encoding.
Owner-retaining checked byte views, relative UTF-8 observations, stable compiled substring patterns and bounded search, cut and comparison operations.
Bounds-proved unaligned little-endian machine-word reads and writes for SIMD and SWAR processing.
Mutable byte buffers with length, construction, copy, and bounds/range-aware access operations.
The ChaCha8 pseudorandom generator: four interleaved eight-round blocks per vector kernel call, byte reads and state encoding.
Unicode scalar values and checked character/code conversions, with range information for safe use.
Columnar leaves over typed arrays, zipped into nested pairs that share their buffers. A length mismatch is None.
Explicit scalar comparison policies, NaN-aware floating orders, and first non-default selection.
Binary64 complex arithmetic, overflow-safe division, polar conversions, and full elementary, trigonometric, hyperbolic, and inverse functions over Data.Float.
Composition of higher-kinded containers with the admitted generic instances.
A constant container that retains its first parameter while ignoring the mapped value parameter.
An RFC 6265 cookie jar as an immutable value: store the cookies responses set and choose the cookies a request sends.
Shared declarations for List, Option, and Result. Their public homes add operations and instances; this module breaks declaration-order cycles.
Civil date values, validation, parsing/formatting, and calendar calculations.
Bounds-checked ELF32 and ELF64 (little/big-endian) parser for headers, segments, sections, symbols, relocations, dynamic tables and zlib-compressed sections.
Finite enumeration and the class behind inclusive range literals, including an explicit next element for a step.
Exact finite domain enumeration for algebraic data, records, and compile-time state-machine action parameters.

Binary64 mathematics: roundings, roots, exponentials, logarithms, powers, trigonometric, hyperbolic and special functions (erf, Gamma, Bessel) and FMA as branch-free kernels, bit-identical on every target.
The opt-in collection-literal vocabulary used to interpret [elements] at the expected container type.
The opt-in map-literal vocabulary used to interpret {key => value} at the expected container type.
Hashing vocabulary and admitted hash implementations for keys.
Hash maps with explicit key constraints, lookup/update, and map-style combination operations.
The identity container and its generic abstraction instances.
Mathematical signed integers, arithmetic, division/remainder, formatting support, and explicit conversions.
Validated IP addresses, parsing/rendering, and address-family vocabulary.
The JSON value representation shared by parsers, renderers, codecs, and structured observability.
Finite strict lists: construction, transformation, filtering, splitting, searching, folds, and collection instances.
Bounds-checked Mach-O 32/64 (little/big-endian) and Universal/Fat binary parser for load commands, segments, sections, symbols and dylibs.
Fixed-width and target-sized scalar operations. Names make checked, wrapping, or saturating overflow policy explicit.
Ordered maps with comparison constraints, lookup, insertion, removal, traversal, and collection-literal support.
Fast keyed 64-bit non-cryptographic hash with persistent streaming state, one-shot byte/string fast paths and MapHashable typed comparable hashing.
Matrix construction, shape checks, indexing, transformation, and arithmetic operations.
A fixed-length mutable array whose slots always hold values, with copying freeze and thaw against the immutable Array.
An ordered mutable map: a degree-8 B-tree whose nodes are indices into one pooled set of slot arrays, with floor, ceiling, range folds, pop-min/max and a structural verifier.
An ordered mutable set: the pooled B-tree with a Unit value per member.
A dynamic bitset in 64-bit words: test/set/toggle, popcount, next-set-bit scanning, and word-at-a-time union, intersection and difference.
A double-ended queue as a power-of-two ring buffer: amortised O(1) push and pop at both ends and O(1) indexing.
A mutable hash set: the HashTable with a Unit value per member.
A mutable hash table after SwissTable and F14: 8-slot chunks with 7-bit tags matched eight at a time, a 64-bit finalizer over the Hash digest, and overflow counts that make deletion tombstone-free.
A 4-ary priority queue with its ordering fixed at construction: O(log n) push and pop, O(1) peek, and an O(n) Floyd build from a list.
In-place heap ordering and indexed repairs through explicit borrowed storage callbacks.
An insertion-ordered hash map: dense entries with a tagged chunk index over them, positional access, O(1) swap-remove and order-keeping shift-remove.
Stable typed list elements, checked membership and movement, detached value access and bounded self-copy.
A bounded least-recently-used cache: a hash table to nodes threaded on a recency list, with O(1) get, put and eviction.
Explicit IEEE floating key policies without global equality or hashing instances.
Explicit absent-map adapters without hidden null handles.
A mutable map with captured key policies and deletion-aware live traversal.
Mutable circular sequences with stable cursors, alias-preserving joins and splits, explicit value ownership and bounded arena growth.
Disjoint sets with union by size and path halving: near-constant find, union and same-set queries, and appendable elements.
A single mutable cell, written in place; not synchronized (TVar is the shared cell).
A growable vector: amortised O(1) push and pop, O(1) indexing, middle insertion and removal, in-place introsort, and copying freeze/thaw against Array.
A curated mutable-container facade. Region-indexed operations carry Mut r; callback-backed heaps and stable linked-list elements have their own module imports.
Mathematical nonnegative integers, exact arithmetic, checked preconditions, and admitted machine conversions.
Immutable IPv4, IPv6, 4-in-6 and zoned addresses, AddrPort pairs and CIDR prefixes with RFC 5952 formatting, containment, overlap and binary codecs.
Lists refined by nonemptiness. The total constructor returns Option; transferred operations must preserve the predicate.
Total nonzero-number constructors. The NonZero type is also available through the arithmetic vocabulary for safe divisors.
Optional values with None and Some, plus combinators for propagating or consuming absence.
The LT, EQ, and GT comparison result vocabulary and its instances.
Platform path values and composition/conversion operations used by filesystem and process APIs.
Bounds-checked PE32, PE32+ and COFF binary parser for headers, data directories, sections, COFF symbols, imports and exports.
Partial producer vocabulary, distinct from codata whose next observation is guaranteed productive.
Pseudorandom sources as values (PCG and ChaCha8) and their distributions: bounded integers, floats, permutations, ziggurat normal and exponential variates, and Zipf.
Rational numbers with explicit denominator/error policy and arithmetic operations.
Success and named failure values, error-aware transformations, partitioning, and sequencing instances.
Indexed binary search with monotone predicates, insertion positions and effectful three-way comparisons.
Ordered sets and their membership, combination, difference, and conversion operations.
Lists refined by sortedness, with construction and combination that preserve ordering.
Pure typed SQL values, NULLs, named parameters, isolation levels, column metadata, errors and checked row scanners.
Immutable UTF-8 text with bounded-stack construction and joining, scalar/span decoding, SIMD scalar counting, slicing and comparison. Byte conversions preserve immutability.
In-memory string-oriented I/O utilities with explicit state and error results.
Immutable O(n log n) suffix arrays over raw bytes with binary-search lookup, regex search and checked versioned binary serialization.
Interned symbols with identity equality, deterministic spelling order, and String conversions.
Target/platform and worker vocabulary used by the compiler-supported runtime and target examples.
Immutable row-major tensors with checked runtime shapes of any rank.
Calendar-aware spans applied to dates, wall-clock times, date-times and instants, with explicit overflow results.
Civil calendar dates with validated construction, weekday and ordinal queries, and day arithmetic.
Civil date and wall-clock time pairs without a time zone.
Exact signed elapsed-time durations with nanosecond precision and checked arithmetic.
Monotonic clock readings for measuring elapsed time; never related to the civil calendar.
Fixed offsets from UTC with validated ranges.
Calendar-aware spans that keep each unit (years through nanoseconds), with balancing and rounding.
Civil wall-clock times of day with nanosecond precision.
Instants on the Unix time line with nanosecond precision and checked arithmetic.
Span units, rounding modes and the shared rounding kernel.
The seven days of the week with ordering and offset arithmetic.
POSIX TZ rule strings: parsing and evaluating standard/daylight transition rules.
Shared vocabulary for time zones: transitions, ambiguity and disambiguation policies.
Reading TZif time zone files (RFC 9636) into checked transition tables.
Time zones: offsets for instants, resolution of civil times, and fixed or rule-based zones.
Arithmetic, differences and rounding on zoned date-times.
Instants paired with a time zone, with civil field access.
Time values, durations, and conversions with explicit units and admitted ranges.
Unicode scalar and numeric classification, simple case mappings, fold cycles and checked locale overrides.
Named Unicode category, script and property tables with deterministic catalog observations.
Immutable Unicode range tables with checked construction, exact membership and copied observations.
Generated Unicode property, case and folding data with a pinned version and source provenance.
Versioned Unicode classification, simple case mappings, fold cycles, named tables and checked custom ranges.
Immutable 128-bit identifiers with RFC 9562 text, ordering and explicit version 7 state.
Unboxed 128-bit integers with checked, wrapping and saturating arithmetic, bit operations, numeric conversions and explicit overflow policies.
Bit lengths, byte reversal, signed rotations and checked carry/borrow, wide multiply, divide and remainder operations over fixed and native-width words.
Inspectable scalar checksum sinks, generic byte writers and bounded reader-to-Adler-32 copying with advanced source continuations.
Region-delimited bump arenas with O(1) fast escape (with-arena, arena-abort) and typed byte-budget boundaries (with-arena-budget, BudgetError).
ASCII85 encoding writers and decoding byte readers with explicit finalization, bounded read-ahead and sticky stream errors.
Explicitly finalized Base32 encoding writers and bounded decoding readers with precise errors, retained cursors and sticky failures.
Explicitly finalized Base64 writers and bounded decoding readers with sticky errors and isolated output chunks.
Benchmark case execution and timing/reporting helpers over runtime clocks.
Explicit fixed and variable binary stream codecs preserving progress and advanced handles after failures.
Byte-stream events with signed progress, simultaneous failures, shared advanced continuations and explicit transfer capabilities.
Initialized opaque continuation cells whose allocation, observation and replacement require their I/O region.
Exact bounded byte scans shared by buffered input and token splitters.
Buffered byte reading with explicit advanced handles and independently owned observations.
Buffered byte output with sticky failures, exact partial progress and independently owned reservations.
Buffered input and output components with explicit independent advanced handles.
Runtime monotonic and wall-clock readings under an I/O capability. Clocks are not ambient compile-time inputs.
Native single-place shared variables with FIFO handoff, blocking take/put/read/swap, nonblocking operations, and cancellable waits through the task scheduler.
Shipped task/worker vocabulary supplementing the compiler-installed structured scope and join operations.
Coverage collection/reporting utilities with explicit runtime and source metadata.
CRC-32 stream writers and bounded copying into an inspectable checksum state.
Inspectable CRC-64 states, generic byte writers and bounded reader-to-checksum copying with advanced source continuations.
Ed25519, X25519 and AES key generation and random-nonce GCM over the operating system random source.
Bounded CSV readers and writers with explicit continuation, record counts, position tracking and advanced handles after failures.
Region-scoped live metrics registry (Int, Float, String, Map, Func) with deterministic sorted JSON snapshots and /debug/vars HTTP response adapter.
Convenience filesystem operations built on the lower-level filesystem API.
Filesystem walking/search utilities with the module's traversal and error policy.
Incremental raw DEFLATE streaming readers and writers over Effect.Stream with sync flush and preset dictionaries.
Inspectable FNV hashing sinks, generic byte-writer composition and bounded reader-to-hash copying with advanced continuations.
Filesystem reads/writes, directory and metadata operations, with Path values and named Result errors.
Streaming Go gob encoders and decoders over Effect.Stream preserving type IDs across multi-message streams.
Hexadecimal encoding writers, decoding readers and formatted dump sinks with explicit continuations and sticky errors.
HTTP/1.1 and TLS 1.3 HTTPS listener/socket servers with keep-alive, size limits and ServeMux dispatch, plus a TLS/CookieJar/redirect-aware HTTP client.
HTTP/1.1 wire request/response dumping, strict chunked codecs, hop-by-hop header stripping, and HTTP/HTTPS ReverseProxy forwarding.
Bounded HTTP/1.1 and TLS 1.3 HTTPS client operations with response framing, header helpers, and named errors.
In-memory HTTP ResponseRecorder, request builder and loopback wire/socket testing helpers.
A worked configuration-reading API over real filesystem bytes; parse-config treats a nonempty payload as configuration.
Structured log operations and records with runtime capability/effect accounting.
Operating-system entropy seed generation for Data.MapHash.
Inspectable MD5 states, generic digest sinks and bounded reader-to-hash copying for legacy formats.
Encoded-word and header decoding with explicit charset reader capabilities, typed errors and advanced writer continuations.
Explicit shared multipart sessions with borrowed byte I/O capabilities.
TCP client sockets, TCP listeners (listen/accept), UDP send, address values, named errors, and runtime effects.
Validated envelope output through explicit advanced writer continuations, bounded chunks and linear short-write draining.
One-shot and live subprocesses, command arguments/environment additions, pipes, exit codes, and this process's arguments.
Pseudo-terminal-backed child processes, terminal I/O, and lifecycle operations.
Incremental quoted-printable readers and writers with explicit binary policy, partial progress and sticky errors.
Pseudorandom sources seeded from operating-system entropy.
Runtime entropy/random utilities with explicit effectful access.
Zero-overhead lexical reader capabilities (Read and TaggedRead), with ask, asks, local, and type-changing with-reader scoping that preserve purity.
Hostname/address resolution through the runtime, with named failure results.
Effectful JSON-RPC and gob-RPC TCP listener servers, clients, and HTTP POST JSON-RPC handler over Effect.Net and Effect.Http.Server.
Byte-preserving token splitters with explicit absent, empty and final token states.
Advanced byte-stream tokenization with bounded buffers, fresh tokens and explicit checked protocol failures.
The direct, Result, and Option do providers. One lexical provider/container is selected per definition.
Inspectable SHA-1 states, generic digest sinks and bounded reader-to-hash copying for legacy formats.
Inspectable SHA-224/SHA-256 states, generic digest sinks and bounded reader-to-hash copying with advanced source continuations.
Inspectable SHA-3/SHAKE states, generic digest sinks, bounded reader-to-hash copying and SHAKE output as a generic reader.
Inspectable SHA-384/SHA-512/SHA-512/t states, generic digest sinks and bounded reader-to-hash copying with advanced source continuations.
Operating-system signal vocabulary and runtime operations with explicit error/effect handling.
An SMTP client over sockets and TLS 1.3 (implicit SMTPS and RFC 3207 STARTTLS) with explicit client state, HELO fallback, PLAIN/CRAM-MD5 authentication, envelope, data, quit and send-mail.
Capability-explicit SQL driver protocol, STM-backed connection pooling, prepared statements, transactions, retries and an in-memory transactional driver.
A bounded first-in first-out queue for transactions: a write waits while the queue is at capacity, a read waits while it is empty.
A transactional variable that is either empty or full: take waits while empty, put waits while full. The building block for handoff and mutual exclusion inside transactions.
An unbounded first-in first-out queue for transactions, as two lists so that writers and readers touch different variables.
A counting semaphore for transactions: wait takes a permit or retries, signal returns one.

Software transactional memory: TVar cells, composable STM transactions run by atomically, retry and or-else for blocking and choice, and the STM do provider. The transaction algorithm is Cinch source over inline target IR.
Positional byte writers, signed cursor movement and streaming at a base offset.
Positional byte sources, immutable bounded sections, signed seeks and sequential reader adapters.
Composable byte readers and writers with explicit continuation state, memory and descriptor adapters, limits, mirrors, and exact or bulk transfers.
RFC 3164 and RFC 5424 syslog message formatting, facility/severity priorities, Effect.Log sink bridge, and UDP/TCP network writers.
Immutable in-memory MapFs with synthesized directories, path validation, globbing, subtrees and filesystem conformance checks.
Choice-stream property testing and native-speed state-machine simulation with automatic integrated shrinking (Hegel / Hypothesis / Hedgehog style).
Stream fault-injection, logging and conformance-testing adapters over Effect.Stream.
Deterministic property-based testing engine with Arbitrary instances over Data.Rand.
A subprocess-based test runner and named test-result/report vocabulary.
Typed short-circuiting algebraic error effect (Throw e) with cross-call cooperative bubbling, throw, catch, and try-throw.
The system time zone database and the current system zone.
Typed readers for the system and monotonic clocks.
Effectful TLS 1.3 client and server connections over Effect.Net sockets with OS entropy and clock-checked certificate verification.
Scoped tracing/span vocabulary and context propagation tied to the runtime identity.
Operating-system user and group lookups (current user, by name/UID/GID, supplementary group IDs) over Prim.Sys and Effect.Process.
Secure UUID generation with explicit serialized version 7 ownership.
Small reusable function operations such as identity, composition, argument manipulation, and application.
Immutable factories for the ordered 256-color Plan 9 and 216-color WebSafe palettes.
Color representations, conversion models and immutable palettes with first-nearest lookup.
Composite rasters with Src and Over, masks and uniform colors, and dither onto palettes, with a vector Over kernel.
Decode and encode GIF images and animations: palettes, transparency, delays, disposal, looping and interlace.
Baseline and progressive JPEG decoding to YCbCr, gray, RGB or CMYK planes, and baseline encoding, with vector IDCT, FDCT, Huffman and colour kernels.
PNG decoding of every color type, depth and interlace method with SIMD scanline reconstruction, and PNG encoding.
Gray, gray-alpha, RGB, RGBA and paletted rasters at eight and sixteen bits with pixel access and RGBA conversion.
The implicit, curated base surface available in every program. This facade re-exports selected defining modules; it is not the whole library.

Leaf inline-LLVM scalar machine primitives (fixed-width wrapping/saturating/overflow/bitwise/shift/rotate/bitscan/comparison/conversion operations and word-size bridges), re-exported through Data.Machine and shared directly by Data.Char, Data.Bytes, and Data.String.

The Darwin half of the syscall layer: libSystem calls bound with foreign import ccall (open, read, write, close, lseek, fstat, mkdir, unlink, rename, fsync, getpid), with the -1 result mapped to a named error read from the thread error slot.

The Linux half of the syscall layer: prim bodies that issue syscall with the pinned number per architecture (x86_64 and aarch64), with the kernel negative result mapped to the same named errors as the Darwin module.

The floor under Prim.Sys: the same entry names and the same named errors as the real backends, with every entry point answering Err SysIoError. It is what a target with no backend yet gets, and it keeps the prelude surface from being empty there.

The syscall layer for the compile target under one name: conditional imports and re-exports select Prim.Sys.Darwin on a Darwin target, Prim.Sys.Linux on a Linux target, and the portable floor everywhere else, so a caller imports one module and never names an operating system.

Leaf inline-LLVM 128-bit SIMD lane primitives and target-guarded hardware AES/CLMUL instructions (AES-NI, ARMv8 AES, PCLMULQDQ, PMULL) with portable fallbacks, re-exported through Data.Wide and shared directly by Data.String.
Equality/inequality class vocabulary. Instances live with their types.
Ordering vocabulary and comparison helpers. State all required dictionaries explicitly; superclass entailment is not implicit.
Portable SIMD Adler-32 with bounded machine-word segments, persistent states, network-order digests and checked versioned checkpoints.
Command-line argument processing and its named value/error vocabulary.
ASCII85 text, caller-buffer and incremental codecs with consumed-input progress, checked source offsets, SIMD groups and control-run scanning.
ASN.1 value trees with a strict DER decoder and canonical DER encoder, including explicit and implicit tags and times.
Configurable Base32 byte alphabets and padding, SIMD codecs, prefix/caller-buffer operations and persistent incremental states.
Configurable Base64 byte alphabets, padding and strict trailing bits, SIMD codecs, persistent states and checked caller buffers.
Base64 encoding/decoding over bytes with explicit invalid-input results.
Typed scalar, floating-point, complex and aggregate binary layouts with checked buffers, exact sizes and packed array kernels.
Little- and big-endian integer encoding, checked buffer access, and signed/unsigned varints.
An efficient text-construction vocabulary for assembling many fragments before rendering.
Decompress concatenated bzip2 streams with table-driven Huffman decoding and verified block and stream CRCs.
Incremental Adler-32, CRC-32 and CRC-64 checksums with explicit reflected polynomials.
Encoding/decoding signatures and codec helpers with explicit failure results.
HTTP cookies: parse Set-Cookie and Cookie header lines, serialize cookies as Set-Cookie values and validate them.
Prepared reflected polynomial tables, persistent CRC-32 states and table-checked binary checkpoints.
Immutable SIMD-built polynomial tables, slicing-by-eight CRC-64, persistent states, network-order digests and table-checked checkpoints.
Configurable Unicode-delimited and lossless byte CSV records, checked partial results, positions and incremental parser state.
CSV parsing/rendering with explicit field, record, and malformed-input handling.
Digest and HMAC operations over bytes. Availability of a legacy digest is not a recommendation for a security protocol.
POSIX lexical relative paths, locality tests, filesystem-name conversion and search-list splitting.
RFC 1951 raw DEFLATE compression (hash-chain LZ77 and Package-Merge dynamic/fixed Huffman) and bounded decompression with preset dictionaries.
Persistent FNV states with reset, network-order digests, numeric observations and checked versioned binary checkpoints.
Incremental 32-, 64- and 128-bit FNV-1 and FNV-1a hashing with explicit wrapping arithmetic.
Wire-compatible Go gob binary encoder and decoder for primitives, slices, arrays, maps and structs with stateful type-descriptor reuse.
Whole-buffer gzip member encoding, checked decompression and concatenated members.
SIMD hexadecimal text/byte codecs, prefix-preserving decoding, append and destination operations, and formatted byte dumps.
HTML text/byte escaping, complete HTML5 character references, exact escaped sizing and SIMD/SWAR scanning.
Context-aware auto-escaping HTML template engine over Text.Template and Text.Html with typed safe content wrappers for HTML, attributes, URLs, JS, CSS and srcset.
Pure HTTP/1.1 wire parsing/rendering, chunked transfer coding, status texts, canonical headers, forms and Go 1.22 ServeMux pattern routing.
Exact decimal rounding and shortest finite binary32 JSON coefficients, with preserved signed zero and midpoint comparisons.
Typed JSON codecs for records, persistent maps, explicit key capabilities, machine integers, binary buffers and exact binary32/binary64 values.
Owned dynamic JSON trees, separate encoding and decoding descriptors, typed payloads and bounded construction.
Explicit legacy codec policy and descriptor bridges over owned dynamic values.
Owned JSON documents and navigation tapes, raw number spellings, exact numeric values and input-bearing errors, resumable lexical state and byte-preserving formatting.
JSON parsing and rendering over Data.Json, with explicit errors and builder-based output.
Lexer toolkit: tokens, spans, and lexical errors for grammar and parser clients.
Variable-width-code LZW compression and decompression in either bit order, as used by GIF, TIFF and PDF.
Parse and format RFC 5322 mail addresses, read message header blocks and parse header dates, with SIMD atom scanning.
MD5 for legacy interoperability, with persistent states, little-endian digests and checked binary checkpoints.
Byte-preserving media types, encoded words, immutable parameter maps and explicit extension registries.
Multipart wire primitives over arbitrary bytes, exact multi-value headers and explicit delimiter observations.
Declarative option specifications, short/long forms, conversion, positionals, usage, and named parse errors.
OTLP/JSON record construction/rendering for structured log/trace data and trace-context helpers.
Parser combinator toolkit over the lexer/scanner vocabulary.
Portable slash-path lexical operations and checked shell patterns with reusable compiled matchers and exact SIMD scans.
Owned byte-preserving envelope blocks, persistent headers, exact malformed-input recovery and bounded payload encoding.
Punycode (RFC 3492) encoding and decoding, and ASCII-compatible host names with xn-- labels.
Quoted-printable byte encoding and decoding with checked line wrapping, escape and malformed-input policies.
Regular-expression parsing/matching and replacement under the module's admitted regex language.
Pure JSON-RPC 1.0/2.0 (single, notification, batch) and length-prefixed gob-RPC wire codecs, envelopes, and standard error codes.
Scanning primitives over input text and the shared position/error vocabulary.
SHA-1 for legacy interoperability, with a four-lane SIMD schedule, persistent states and checked binary checkpoints.
Portable SHA-224/SHA-256 with generated SIMD schedules, persistent states, network-order digests and checked binary checkpoints.
SHA3-224/256/384/512, SHAKE128/256 and cSHAKE128/256 over a register-resident Keccak permutation, with persistent sponges, output readers and checkpoints.
Portable SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 with two-lane SIMD schedules, native rotates, persistent states and checked binary checkpoints.
Shell-style word splitting/joining; this is data parsing, not execution of a shell command.
Rendering values as String. The concrete formatting helpers are re-exported by Prelude; import this module for Show itself.
SMTP without a connection: reply state machine, command validation, extensions, dot-stuffing and PLAIN/CRAM-MD5 exchanges.
Explicit-base and width-aware integer codecs, exact decimal and hexadecimal float parsing and formatting, complex parsing/formatting and Go string/rune quoting.
Elastic tabstops: align tab-separated cells into padded columns, with escapes, HTML-aware widths, right alignment and incremental flushing.
Read V7, USTAR, PAX and GNU tape archives and write USTAR or PAX archives, with SIMD header checksums.
Data-driven text templates: pipelines, control actions, definitions, builtins and printf over dynamic values.
Text-protocol framing: lines, canonical MIME headers, status responses and dot encoding for HTTP, SMTP and mail.
ISO 8601 and friendly duration text for spans and exact durations, printing and parsing.
ISO 8601 extended format and RFC 3339 printing and parsing for dates, times, date-times and timestamps.
RFC 2822/5322 internet-message date-time printing and parsing.
RFC 9557 date-time text with bracketed time zone annotations for zoned values.
Shared byte cursor, digit readers and digit writers for the time text modules.
POSIX strftime/strptime-style formatting and parsing over broken-down time fields.
Offset and zoned-value text functions.
The module's supported TOML parsing/rendering surface and explicit unsupported/malformed cases.
URI parsing, rendering, components, and validation/error vocabulary.
Checked percent codecs for URL components, exact escaped sizing and optional UTF-8 text views.
Structured URL failures with original byte offsets, context, diagnostics and explicit causes.
URL host IP-literal and port validation with explicit IPv6 and zone rules.
Immutable URL components, raw encoding hints, rendering and independent copied observations.

Persistent byte-preserving query multimaps with deterministic encoding, checked parsing and copied observations.
URL reference resolution, lexical path joining and copied persistent URL updates.
